chapter: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
title: Lips Page band personnel and the "Lover Man" theme
summary: He names Ike Quebec, Gene Ammons, Bennie Green and others, and says the band's unnamed theme later became "Lover Man," titled by Jimmy Davis.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x:
who could rob one another...
Now, we had Ike Quebec and Dave Young in the reeds; Floyd Horsecollar Williams, first alto... Let me see, who else did we have? Ah, Gene Ammons. Then we had Bennie Green on trombone. We had Vic Dickinson. We had Charlie Redman. We had two other guys, but I forget their names, who were good trumpet players. Abe Bolar on bass. A boy named Parker on drums. Oh, man, it was a hell of... Ike Quebec...
Yeah, that was a strong band.
It was a helluva band, let me tell you. It's too bad we didn't record. (?)I had the arrangements.(?) And the theme song, we had a little thing up there... It wasn't "Lover Man" yet. [SINGS THEME]
Is that what you played as a theme?
Yeah, that was the theme song for the band.

Yeah, but it wasn't "Lover Man" yet. Because I just sketched it out, you know. It was great. Jimmy Davis came up with the title of "Lover Man." I said, "Let's do something...give it some kind of rhythm."
